key_insight: A large open-weight LLM, Llama 3.3 70B, could automatically identify complex PCI features from catheterization reports with strong overall performance, especially for clearly documented variables.
clinical_relevance: This suggests locally deployable LLMs may help scale cardiovascular phenotyping from unstructured cath reports and reduce manual abstraction workload.
method: Manually annotated cath reports from 3 hospitals in Yale New Haven Health
Compared 3 open-weight LLMs: Llama 3.3 70B, Meditron-7B, and BioMistral-7B
Evaluated PCI detection plus extraction of 6 complex PCI features
evidence_signal: In 1,412 notes, 596 were PCI reports; Llama 3.3 70B achieved 100.0% sensitivity and 93.8% specificity for PCI identification, and 97.7% sensitivity with 83.9% accuracy for complex PCI classification across 590 evaluable PCI reports.
watch_item: Performance varied by site and was weaker for features requiring interpretation across multiple procedural details, so local validation is important before deployment.
paper_title: Automated Identification of Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention from Cardiac Catheterization Reports Using Large Language Models
